facts.text: The male rose robin has a distinctive pink breast and abdomen, with dark grey head, throat, back and tail.
facts.quote: The male rose robin has a pink breast and abdomen, with dark grey head, throat, back and tail.

facts.text: The female rose robin is plain-coloured, pale grey-brown above and grey-white underneath with small white marks on the wings.
facts.quote: The female is plain-coloured; pale grey-brown above, and grey-white underneath, with small white marks on the wings and over the bill.

facts.text: Both the male and female make a tick call.
facts.quote: Both the male and female make a tick call.

facts.text: Unlike other robins, it does not return to the same branch while foraging.
facts.quote: Unlike other robins, the rose robin does not return to the same branch while foraging.

facts.text: Its prey includes caterpillars, wasps, cicadas, jewel beetles, weevils, flies and ants.
facts.quote: Prey consists of a variety of spiders and insects, including caterpillars, wasps, bugs such as cicadas and chinch bugs, beetles such as jewel beetles, leaf beetles, leaf-eating beetles and weevils, flies and ants.

facts.text: Breeding runs from September to January, with one or two broods raised.
facts.quote: Breeding season is from September to January with one or two broods raised.

facts.text: Two or three dull white eggs tinted bluish, greyish or brownish are laid, and cuckoos sometimes parasitise the nest.
facts.quote: Two or three dull white eggs tinted bluish, greyish or brownish, and splotched with dark grey-brown, are laid.

facts.text: The rose robin's nest, decorated with lichen on the outside, sits high in the fork of a large tree, some 10–20 m (33–66 ft) above the ground.
facts.quote: The nest is generally situated in the fork of a large tree some 10–20 m (33–66 ft) above the ground.

facts.text: It is named for its colour: the specific epithet comes from the Latin roseus, meaning pink.
facts.quote: It was first described by ornithologist John Gould in 1840, with its specific epithet derived from the Latin roseus 'pink'.

facts.text: Its tail is black with white tips, and it has a small black bill and eyes.
facts.quote: its tail black with white tips. The underparts and shoulder are white.
